A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Articulate-Anything paper, with 24 complete, readable pages including Appendices A.1–A.8. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish matching scientific content, figures, tables and equations.

before.justification: v3 reports original PartNet-Mobility experiments, ablations, mesh-reconstruction measurements and real-robot manipulation results in Sections 5–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including articulation benchmarks, appendix reconstruction comparisons and real-robot policy evaluations.

M1.justification: The mesh-retrieval, link-placement and joint-prediction pipeline, actor-critic refinement and targeted affordance extraction are identical. Appendix A.8's mesh-generation integration is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same PartNet-Mobility categories, in-the-wild objects, input modalities and four robotic manipulation tasks. Appendix evaluations introduce no coverage differences.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical, including URDFormer Oracle/DINO, Real2Code Oracle, human-annotated robotic assets and the mesh-generation models compared in Appendix A.8.

E3.justification: Evaluation settings are unchanged, including the 50 mm and 0.25 radian success thresholds, seen/unseen category groupings, ablation controls and robotics training protocol.

E4.justification: Both retain identical modality, refinement, in-context-example and VLM-choice ablations, failure analyses, critic-agreement analysis and category breakdowns in the main text and appendices.

E5.justification: Confidence-interval and standard-deviation reporting in Figure 5 and Tables 1–3 is unchanged. Appendix A.3 retains the same disclosure of three random seeds per robotic task.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match. Figure 5 retains 75.0% for Articulate-Anything, 14.6% for URDFormer Oracle, 8.7% for URDFormer DINO and 12.2% for Real2Code Oracle; appendix tables and plots are also identical.

T1.justification: The URDF formulation, losses and link/joint error definitions in Section 3 and Appendix A.1, including Equations (1)–(11), are identical. No formal reasoning is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's four contributions and conclusion retain exactly the same claims about multimodal articulation, program synthesis, iterative refinement and empirical performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of visual grounding, critic overestimation and baseline failures are unchanged. The mesh-retrieval limitation and discussion of difficult small parts and irregular movements also remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, baseline reproduction procedures, robotics training details and mesh-generation instructions are identical. The project website and source-code access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the bibliography and comparisons positioning the work against earlier methods are identical. No cited work or novelty relationship changes.

P1.justification: The marginal arXiv stamp changes from v3 dated 6 February 2025 to v4 dated 2 June 2025. All research prose, headings, terminology and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp is slightly repositioned. All figures, tables, captions and body layout remain identical; rendered pages 2–24 match pixel-for-pixel.

improvement.justification: v4 preserves the same scientific content, empirical evidence, limitations and reproducibility information throughout the main text and appendices. The arXiv stamp and PDF metadata updates do not meaningfully improve or diminish the paper's overall quality.
